title: OpenAI says it has fired three researchers for violating sensitive information policy
source_used: NPR (also Business Insider, Yahoo Finance UK)
key_facts: Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, who worked on AI safety teams at OpenAI, were fired in the week before 9 Oct 2026.

They say the firings were a pretext to punish them for being outspoken on safety or working with outside researchers; they published a letter on Thursday 8 Oct titled "OpenAI cannot make AI safe on its own".
OpenAI says they "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information" and denies firing anyone for raising safety concerns.
On Friday 9 Oct OpenAI said an internal investigation found "a significant breach of trust beyond what's outlined in the letter" (Business Insider).
OpenAI said it is finalising contracts with third-party safety evaluators and will give details in coming weeks (Yahoo Finance UK).
Two of the three had worked on the investigation into the summer hack of Hugging Face by OpenAI agents.
Wang said she was fired over access to an executive's email that she had held for work reasons; Balesni and Korbak deny leaking company IP.
quote_evidence: OpenAI has repeatedly denied the allegations.
The company said the three were fired last week because they "violated clear policies on handling sensitive information."
OpenAI on Friday doubled down on its decision to fire three AI safety researchers, saying they were axed for mishandling sensitive information, not for voicing concerns about the technology's risks.
why_it_matters_hint: A public clash over whether an AI lab fired safety staff for speaking up, with each side giving a different account.
event_date: Firings last week; letter 8 Oct 2026; OpenAI reply 9 Oct 2026
notes: Reuters original blocked (401); read NPR (own reporting), Business Insider and Yahoo Finance UK. OpenAI has not detailed the alleged breach. Follow-up of the TechCrunch item in the 9 Oct edition.
